nodes.label: Elevated hepatobiliary enzymes in a 27-year-old woman
The patient occasionally drank alcohol and had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
The patient was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, her hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Laboratory tests show cholestatic pattern: ALP 1028 U/L, GGT 257 U/L with relatively mild AST/ALT elevation
Imaging identifies an irregular hilar lesion
Liver biopsy reveals PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule occluding interlobular veins and destroying bile ducts
MRI shows hypointense hepatic parenchyma corresponding to the hilar lesion
CT shows contrast enhancement of the hilar lesion except in the isoechoic region
Tumor markers, MRCP/ERCP, immunohistochemistry, and PET-CT have not yet been performed
The metastatic malignancy has an occult primary tumor site that has not yet been identified
Malignant biliary obstruction due to metastatic carcinoma of Müllerian/gynecologic origin (ovarian or endometrial)
Malignant biliary obstruction due to metastatic renal cell carcinoma
Malignant biliary obstruction due to metastatic thyroid carcinoma
Malignant biliary obstruction due to metastatic upper gastrointestinal/pancreaticobiliary adenocarcinoma with aberrant PAX8 expression
Expert pathology and radiology analyses independently state that PAX8 positivity strongly favors a Müllerian/gynecologic primary (ovarian/endometrial)
Specific pending workup includes pelvic imaging, CA125/HE4, WT1/ER/PR/p16, and PET/MRCP for staging
Current imaging and biopsy have not identified a primary tumor site
